questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: Values, in the context of civic education, are best defined as
options: principles or standards that guide acceptable behaviour in society
the total wealth possessed by a nation
laws passed exclusively by the national legislature
punishments given for criminal offences
questions.explanation: Values are the shared principles and standards a society uses to judge what behaviour is acceptable, right, or desirable.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: Being truthful and transparent in one's dealings with others is an example of the value of
options: discipline
obedience
tolerance
honesty
questions.explanation: Honesty is the value of being truthful, transparent, and free from deception in one's words and actions.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: The value that involves the willingness to accept and respect differing views, cultures, or religions is called
options: obedience
justice
discipline
tolerance
questions.explanation: Tolerance means accepting and respecting people's differing beliefs, customs, or opinions, even when they differ from one's own.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: Treating all individuals fairly and giving each person what is rightfully due to them reflects the value of
options: justice
discipline
obedience
tolerance
questions.explanation: Justice involves fair treatment and ensuring that individuals receive what they are rightly entitled to under the law and in society.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: The self-controlled ability to follow rules and maintain orderly conduct reflects the value of
options: honesty
fairness
discipline
tolerance
questions.explanation: Discipline reflects the ability to control one's behaviour and consistently follow established rules and standards of conduct.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: Values are important to human society mainly because they
options: guarantee that every citizen becomes wealthy
provide a shared standard for acceptable conduct, promoting peace and order
eliminate the need for laws entirely
ensure that only one political party governs a country
questions.explanation: Shared societal values create common expectations for behaviour, helping to maintain social order, cooperation, and peaceful coexistence.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: Citizenship is best defined as
options: the ability to speak a country's official language
membership of a particular political party
the legal status of belonging to a particular state, with accompanying rights and duties
the ownership of property within a country
questions.explanation: Citizenship establishes a person's legal membership of a state, granting rights and imposing corresponding duties and obligations.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: Citizenship acquired automatically by virtue of being born within a country's territory, or born to citizen parents, is acquired by
options: marriage alone
registration
birth
naturalization
questions.explanation: Citizenship by birth is granted either through being born on the state's territory (jus soli) or born to citizen parents (jus sanguinis).

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: Citizenship granted to a foreigner through an administrative or legal process, often after meeting residency requirements, without undergoing a full naturalization process, is acquired by
options: conquest
descent alone
birth
registration
questions.explanation: Registration is a simplified legal process by which certain qualifying foreigners, such as those married to citizens, may acquire citizenship.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: Citizenship acquired by a foreigner who fulfils specific legal requirements, such as years of residency and good conduct, through a formal government process, is called
options: annexation
naturalization
registration
birth
questions.explanation: Naturalization is a formal legal process through which a qualified foreign national may be granted full citizenship after meeting set requirements.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: A situation in which an individual simultaneously holds citizenship of two different countries is called
options: expatriation
statelessness
naturalization
dual citizenship
questions.explanation: Dual citizenship occurs when a person is recognised as a citizen of two countries at the same time, subject to each country's laws.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: A common reason for the termination of a person's citizenship of a country is
options: voluntary renunciation or acquisition of another country's citizenship where dual citizenship is prohibited
reaching the age of eighteen
getting married within the country
completing secondary education
questions.explanation: Citizenship may be terminated through voluntary renunciation, or in some legal systems, automatically upon acquiring another country's citizenship where dual citizenship isn't allowed.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: Fundamental Human Rights that guarantee an individual's personal freedoms, such as the right to life and freedom of movement, are classified as
options: political rights
economic rights
social rights
civil rights
questions.explanation: Civil rights protect an individual's basic personal freedoms and legal protections, such as the right to life, liberty, and fair trial.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: Rights that allow citizens to participate in governance, such as the right to vote and contest elections, are classified as
options: social rights
political rights
civil rights
economic rights
questions.explanation: Political rights enable citizens to participate meaningfully in the governance of their country, including voting and holding public office.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: Rights concerned with an individual's ability to work, own property, and engage in trade are classified as
options: social rights
political rights
civil rights
economic rights
questions.explanation: Economic rights protect an individual's ability to earn a livelihood, own property, and participate in economic activities.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: Rights that guarantee access to education, healthcare, and welfare are classified as
options: political rights
economic rights
civil rights
social rights
questions.explanation: Social rights ensure access to essential services such as education, healthcare, and social security that support wellbeing.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: During a state of emergency, a government may lawfully
options: permanently abolish the constitution
temporarily restrict certain fundamental human rights, such as freedom of movement
eliminate the judiciary entirely
transfer all rights to a foreign government
questions.explanation: Constitutions typically allow certain rights to be temporarily limited during a declared state of emergency, to protect public safety and order.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: A duty citizens owe to the state, in return for the protection and rights the state provides, includes
options: avoiding all forms of civic participation
ignoring national symbols and institutions
obeying the laws of the land
refusing to pay any taxes
questions.explanation: Citizens are expected to obey the law as part of their civic duty in exchange for the state's protection of their rights.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: Nationalism, in a civic sense, refers to
options: a strong sense of loyalty, pride, and devotion to one's nation
preference for foreign cultures over one's own
rejection of all forms of national government
loyalty exclusively to one's ethnic group over the nation
questions.explanation: Nationalism reflects deep attachment and loyalty to one's nation, often expressed through pride in its identity, achievements, and unity.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: Programmes such as the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) in Nigeria are designed mainly to promote
options: regional separation between states
exclusive employment of graduates in their home states only
national unity and integration among young citizens from different backgrounds
permanent government employment for all participants
questions.explanation: NYSC deliberately posts graduates to serve in states other than their own, fostering national unity and cross-cultural understanding among Nigerian youth.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: National sports competitions and festivals contribute to nationalism mainly by
options: bringing citizens from diverse backgrounds together in shared national pride
discouraging citizens from supporting their country
dividing citizens according to their state of origin
promoting rivalry between different religions
questions.explanation: Shared national events like sports competitions and festivals unite citizens across ethnic and regional lines, strengthening a common sense of national identity.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: A citizen who actively participates in community development projects is demonstrating
options: human trafficking
electoral malpractice
cultism
civic responsibility
questions.explanation: Civic responsibility involves citizens actively contributing to the wellbeing and development of their communities and country.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: Fairness, as a societal value, is best demonstrated when a person
options: ignores the needs of people outside their family
treats others equitably and without unjust bias or favouritism
favours only their close friends and relatives
acts solely in their own self-interest regardless of others
questions.explanation: Fairness requires treating people equitably, without allowing personal bias or favouritism to distort just outcomes.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: Obedience, as a civic value, refers to
options: blind submission to any instruction regardless of legality
loyalty only to one's immediate family
compliance with lawful instructions, rules, and constituted authority
refusal to follow any rules or regulations
questions.explanation: Obedience as a civic value involves respecting and complying with lawful rules and legitimate authority, not unquestioning submission to anything demanded.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: A country that loses foreign-born residents to naturalization elsewhere may see its own citizenship terminated for those individuals through a process called
options: expatriation
registration
conquest
birth
questions.explanation: Expatriation refers to the formal renunciation or loss of one's original citizenship, often upon acquiring citizenship elsewhere.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: A stateless person is someone who
options: has recently acquired citizenship through naturalization
is not recognised as a citizen by any country under its laws
was born to citizen parents abroad
holds citizenship of two countries at once
questions.explanation: Statelessness occurs when an individual is not considered a national by any state, often leaving them without the legal protections citizenship provides.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: A key benefit of national integration efforts, such as inter-state marriages and mixed-ethnic communities, is
options: increased ethnic rivalry and division
the disappearance of all cultural diversity
weakened ties between different regions of a country
reduced ethnic prejudice and a stronger sense of shared national identity
questions.explanation: Programmes and social practices that mix people from different ethnic backgrounds tend to reduce prejudice and build a stronger shared national identity.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: The right to freedom of expression, allowing citizens to voice opinions without undue government interference, is classified as a
options: civil right
purely economic right
duty rather than a right
purely social right
questions.explanation: Freedom of expression is a fundamental civil right protecting an individual's ability to voice opinions and beliefs without unjust restriction.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: The right to own and dispose of private property is classified mainly as an
options: exclusively political right
exclusively social right
exclusively civil right
economic right
questions.explanation: The right to own, use, and dispose of property is primarily an economic right, supporting an individual's ability to accumulate and manage wealth.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: The right to vote in public elections, exercised once a citizen reaches the legally required age, is classified as a
options: purely civil right
purely economic right
political right
purely social right
questions.explanation: The right to vote enables citizens to participate in choosing their leaders, making it a core political right within a democracy.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: Cultism, as a social problem among young people, refers to
options: membership of a registered political party
membership in secret societies that often engage in violent or unlawful activities
participation in officially recognised student clubs
involvement in religious worship groups
questions.explanation: Cultism describes involvement in secret, often violent societies, particularly prevalent in some school and tertiary institution settings.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: A common cause of cultism among young people is
options: lack of access to social media
strict adherence to school rules
excessive parental supervision
peer pressure and the desire for a sense of belonging or protection
questions.explanation: Many young people join cults due to peer influence and a perceived need for protection, identity, or belonging within their social environment.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: A common consequence of cultism in schools and society is
options: violence, injury, and expulsion of students involved
increased trust between students and teachers
improved academic performance for all members
stronger family relationships
questions.explanation: Cultism is frequently associated with violent clashes, harm to students and others, and disciplinary action such as expulsion from school.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: An effective measure schools can take to prevent cultism is
options: allowing unrestricted, unsupervised gatherings
providing strong guidance and counselling services alongside strict disciplinary policies
ignoring reports of secret society activities
reducing the number of teachers and counsellors
questions.explanation: Guidance, counselling, and clear disciplinary policies help address the root causes of cultism and deter students from joining secret societies.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: Drug abuse is best defined as
options: the correct use of prescribed medication as directed by a doctor
the sale of drugs through licensed pharmacies
the storage of drugs in a home medicine cabinet
the excessive or improper use of drugs, without medical justification, leading to harm
questions.explanation: Drug abuse involves using drugs in excessive amounts or inappropriately, without medical need, resulting in physical, mental, or social harm.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: Commonly abused substances among young people include
options: properly prescribed antibiotics
vitamin supplements taken as prescribed
drinking water and fruit juice
marijuana (cannabis), cocaine, and codeine-based cough syrups
questions.explanation: Substances frequently abused include cannabis, cocaine, and codeine-containing cough syrups, among various other harmful drugs.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: A common cause of drug abuse among youths is
options: sufficient access to counselling services
strong parental guidance and supervision
strict school regulations against substance use
peer pressure and the desire to cope with stress or emotional problems
questions.explanation: Youths often turn to drugs due to peer influence, curiosity, or as a way of coping with personal, social, or emotional difficulties.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: A common consequence of drug abuse on the individual is
options: stronger relationships with family and friends
improved academic and social performance
increased life expectancy
damage to physical and mental health, including addiction
questions.explanation: Drug abuse frequently leads to serious physical and psychological harm, including addiction, impaired judgement, and long-term health damage.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: The Nigerian government agency primarily responsible for combating illicit drug trafficking and abuse is the
options: Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC)
National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA)
National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons (NAPTIP)
Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC)
questions.explanation: The NDLEA is Nigeria's primary agency responsible for enforcing laws against illicit drug trafficking, production, and abuse.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: Human trafficking is best defined as
options: the recruitment of soldiers into the national army
the transportation of goods across international borders
the illegal recruitment, transport, or harbouring of persons for exploitation, such as forced labour or prostitution
the lawful migration of workers with valid travel documents
questions.explanation: Human trafficking involves the illegal movement and exploitation of people, often through deception, coercion, or force, for purposes such as forced labour or sexual exploitation.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: A common cause of human trafficking, especially in developing countries, is
options: widespread access to formal education and employment
excessive government regulation of travel
poverty and the false promise of better job opportunities abroad
strong community awareness of trafficking tactics
questions.explanation: Poverty and desperation for better economic opportunities make individuals vulnerable to traffickers' deceptive promises of employment abroad.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: Traffickers commonly lure victims by
options: openly informing victims of the exploitative conditions they will face
providing genuine, well-paying employment with no hidden conditions
promising lucrative jobs, education, or a better life abroad, then exploiting them upon arrival
requiring victims to undergo formal government vetting first
questions.explanation: Traffickers typically deceive victims with false promises of good jobs or opportunities, only to exploit them once they are transported and isolated.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: A significant consequence of human trafficking on its victims is
options: guaranteed wealth and improved social status
automatic citizenship in the destination country
immediate access to quality healthcare and education
physical, emotional, and psychological trauma, often alongside forced labour or abuse
questions.explanation: Victims of trafficking commonly suffer severe physical and psychological harm, exploitation, and abuse at the hands of traffickers.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: The Nigerian government agency primarily responsible for combating human trafficking is the
options: National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA)
National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons (NAPTIP)
Nigeria Police Force alone
Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC)
questions.explanation: NAPTIP is the specific Nigerian agency mandated to investigate, prosecute, and prevent human trafficking, as well as support victims.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: HIV/AIDS is best described as
options: a viral infection that weakens the immune system, potentially progressing to a severe immunodeficiency syndrome
a common seasonal illness with no serious long-term effects
a bacterial infection curable with a short course of antibiotics
a hereditary condition passed only through family genes
questions.explanation: HIV is a virus that attacks the immune system; if untreated, it can progress to AIDS, a stage of severe immune deficiency.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: A common mode of transmission of HIV is
options: shaking hands with an infected person
casual social contact such as hugging
sharing meals with an infected person
unprotected sexual contact with an infected person
questions.explanation: HIV is primarily transmitted through unprotected sexual contact, contaminated blood, and from mother to child, but not through casual everyday contact.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: An effective method of preventing the spread of HIV is
options: sharing sharp objects such as razors and needles
practising safe sex, including the correct use of condoms
avoiding all contact with infected individuals in public
relying solely on traditional herbal remedies
questions.explanation: Safe sexual practices, including condom use, along with avoiding shared needles, significantly reduce the risk of HIV transmission.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: A significant consequence of HIV/AIDS on families and the economy is
options: an automatic increase in national economic productivity
loss of productive family members and increased healthcare costs, straining household and national resources
guaranteed employment for all affected individuals
a reduction in the need for healthcare services
questions.explanation: HIV/AIDS can significantly reduce a family's income and productivity while increasing healthcare costs, with wider effects on national economic development.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: Stigmatization against People Living With HIV/AIDS (PLWHA) is best addressed through
options: denying PLWHA access to healthcare services
isolating PLWHA from the rest of society completely
spreading further misinformation about how HIV is transmitted
public education and awareness campaigns that promote understanding and reduce discrimination
questions.explanation: Accurate public education helps dispel myths about HIV transmission, reducing fear-based discrimination and supporting the dignity of PLWHA.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: A key reason combating stigmatization of PLWHA is important is that stigma often
options: eliminates the need for HIV prevention programmes
has no effect on public health outcomes at all
encourages more people to seek testing and treatment
discourages people from getting tested or seeking treatment for HIV
questions.explanation: Stigma and discrimination can discourage individuals from seeking HIV testing, counselling, and treatment, worsening public health outcomes.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: A common symptom observed in individuals abusing hard drugs includes
options: sudden changes in behaviour, mood swings, and withdrawal from family and friends
improved physical health and appearance
increased responsibility and reliability
consistent, stable academic performance
questions.explanation: Drug abuse often manifests through noticeable behavioural changes, mood instability, and social withdrawal from family and previously close friends.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: A government intervention effort commonly used to combat drug abuse in schools includes
options: public enlightenment campaigns and guidance counselling programmes
increasing the availability of illicit drugs in the community
ignoring reports of drug use among students
removing all drug-related content from the school curriculum
questions.explanation: Awareness campaigns and school counselling services are key preventive tools used to educate students about the dangers of drug abuse.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: Human trafficking for the purpose of forced labour differs from trafficking for sexual exploitation mainly in that victims are
options: always children in every recorded case
always trafficked internationally, never within a single country
never subjected to any form of abuse
forced to work without fair pay or consent, rather than being sexually exploited
questions.explanation: Trafficking for forced labour compels victims into unpaid or underpaid work against their will, distinct from trafficking specifically for sexual exploitation, though both involve severe exploitation.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: International cooperation to fight human trafficking commonly involves
options: allowing traffickers to operate without any legal consequence
ignoring reports of trafficking across borders
closing all national borders permanently
cross-border intelligence sharing and joint law enforcement operations
questions.explanation: Since trafficking often crosses international borders, countries cooperate through intelligence sharing and joint operations to combat the crime effectively.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: A protective measure to reduce vulnerability to human trafficking is
options: public awareness campaigns warning of trafficking tactics and providing legitimate opportunities
reducing school enrolment in vulnerable communities
restricting access to all information about trafficking risks
discouraging community reporting of suspicious recruitment offers
questions.explanation: Educating the public about trafficking tactics, alongside offering genuine opportunities, helps reduce individuals' vulnerability to being deceived by traffickers.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: HIV testing and counselling services are important mainly because they
options: help individuals know their status early and access appropriate care and support
are only useful for people already diagnosed with AIDS
have no bearing on preventing mother-to-child transmission
increase the spread of the virus within communities
questions.explanation: Early testing and counselling allow individuals to learn their HIV status, access treatment promptly, and take steps to prevent further transmission.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: Mother-to-child transmission of HIV can be significantly reduced through
options: exclusive reliance on traditional birth attendants with no medical support
antiretroviral treatment during pregnancy, delivery, and breastfeeding
refusing to test pregnant women for HIV
avoiding all forms of prenatal healthcare
questions.explanation: Appropriate antiretroviral therapy for HIV-positive mothers substantially lowers the risk of transmitting the virus to their children.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: A key challenge in tackling cultism in tertiary institutions is
options: strong, unified opposition to cultism from all students
full cooperation of cult members with school authorities
the complete absence of any cult activities in universities
the secretive nature of cult groups, making detection and prosecution difficult
questions.explanation: Cult groups typically operate secretly, using coded rituals and loyalty oaths, which makes it difficult for authorities to detect and prosecute members.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: Government legislation banning secret cult activities in Nigerian institutions is intended mainly to
options: provide a legal basis for prosecuting and deterring cult membership and activities
encourage more students to join secret societies
reduce funding for guidance and counselling units
eliminate the need for school disciplinary committees
questions.explanation: Anti-cultism laws provide the legal framework needed to investigate, prosecute, and deter individuals from joining or promoting secret cult societies.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: A broader societal consequence of widespread drug abuse is
options: stronger family and community cohesion
improved national productivity and economic growth
a decrease in the demand for healthcare services
increased crime rates and strain on healthcare and social services
questions.explanation: Widespread drug abuse often correlates with rising crime, as well as increased burdens on healthcare, rehabilitation, and social welfare systems.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: Responsible parenthood is best described as
options: having as many children as biologically possible
providing only financial support with no emotional guidance
the conscious effort by parents to provide adequately for the physical, emotional, and moral needs of their children
leaving the upbringing of children entirely to schools
questions.explanation: Responsible parenthood involves deliberately ensuring children's overall wellbeing, including their physical care, emotional support, and moral upbringing.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: A key role of parents under responsible parenthood is
options: avoiding any form of discipline entirely
discouraging children from attending school
providing discipline and moral guidance to their children
leaving all financial provision to the government
questions.explanation: Responsible parents are expected to provide appropriate discipline and moral guidance, helping shape their children's character and values.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: Responsible parenthood contributes to family stability mainly by
options: increasing family conflict and instability
encouraging children to fend for themselves from a young age
reducing parental involvement in children's lives
fostering a secure, nurturing environment that supports children's healthy development
questions.explanation: When parents responsibly provide care, guidance, and support, families tend to be more stable, benefiting children's overall development.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: A consequence of irresponsible parenthood on child development can include
options: strong emotional stability and resilience
excellent academic performance in every case
a complete absence of any behavioural challenges
poor moral upbringing, neglect, and increased vulnerability to social vices
questions.explanation: Irresponsible parenting, marked by neglect or poor guidance, can leave children vulnerable to poor moral development and involvement in social vices.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: Youth restiveness is often linked to irresponsible parenthood mainly because
options: neglected or poorly guided youths may turn to negative influences and antisocial behaviour
youth restiveness has no connection to family upbringing
restiveness is caused solely by government policy
responsible parenting always leads directly to restiveness
questions.explanation: Youths who lack proper parental guidance and support are more susceptible to negative peer influences, frustration, and restive or antisocial behaviour.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: Traffic regulations are best described as
options: laws governing international trade agreements
rules and guidelines governing the safe and orderly use of roads by drivers and pedestrians
rules for the registration of political parties
guidelines for broadcasting on national television
questions.explanation: Traffic regulations establish the rules that road users, including drivers and pedestrians, must follow to ensure safety and order on the roads.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: Road signs that instruct road users on mandatory actions, such as 'Stop' or 'No Entry', are classified as
options: regulatory signs
informative signs
guide signs
warning signs
questions.explanation: Regulatory road signs communicate mandatory rules that road users must obey, such as speed limits or prohibited manoeuvres.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: Road signs that provide useful information to road users, such as directions or the location of facilities, are classified as
options: prohibitory signs
informative signs
warning signs
regulatory signs
questions.explanation: Informative road signs give helpful guidance to road users, such as distances, directions, or nearby amenities, without imposing legal obligations.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: Road signs that alert drivers to potential hazards ahead, such as a sharp bend or pedestrian crossing, are classified as
options: informative signs
guide signs
warning signs
regulatory signs
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert road users to upcoming hazards or changes in road conditions, encouraging caution.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: A common cause of road traffic accidents is
options: strict adherence to speed limits
reckless driving, such as speeding and disregarding traffic signs
proper use of seatbelts by all occupants
regular vehicle maintenance
questions.explanation: Reckless driving behaviours, including excessive speed and ignoring traffic regulations, are leading causes of road traffic accidents.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: The Nigerian government agency primarily responsible for managing traffic and enforcing road safety regulations on federal highways is the
options: National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons (NAPTIP)
Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC)
Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC)
National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA)
questions.explanation: The FRSC is Nigeria's dedicated agency for road traffic administration, safety education, and enforcement of traffic regulations.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: Inter-personal relations refer to
options: the legal rules governing international trade
the relationship between a country and international organisations only
the interactions and connections between individuals or groups within a society
the internal structure of a single political party
questions.explanation: Inter-personal relations describe the ways individuals and groups within a community interact, cooperate, and sometimes conflict with one another.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: A common cause of communal conflict between different ethnic or community groups is
options: disputes over land, resources, or perceived marginalisation
strong, effective conflict resolution mechanisms
excessive cooperation between neighbouring communities
equal and fair distribution of resources
questions.explanation: Communal conflicts commonly arise from competition over land and resources, or from a sense of unfair treatment or marginalisation between groups.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: An effective mechanism for resolving communal conflicts is
options: allowing conflicts to escalate without intervention
the use of violence to suppress one party completely
ignoring the underlying causes of the conflict
dialogue and mediation involving respected community leaders
questions.explanation: Peaceful dialogue and mediation, often facilitated by trusted community or traditional leaders, are effective ways to address and resolve communal disputes.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: A key skill required for promoting peace in inter-communal relations is
options: suppressing all forms of dialogue between groups
refusal to listen to opposing perspectives
effective communication and empathy toward differing viewpoints
encouraging division among community members
questions.explanation: Building peace requires skills such as active listening, empathy, and open communication to understand and address differing perspectives.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: Parents contribute to responsible parenthood by providing financial support mainly to
options: avoid any involvement in their children's upbringing
accumulate personal wealth unrelated to the family
replace the need for emotional support entirely
meet their children's basic needs, such as food, shelter, and education
questions.explanation: Financial provision by parents is aimed at ensuring children's basic needs, including nutrition, shelter, healthcare, and education, are adequately met.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: A regulatory road sign shaped as an octagon with the word 'STOP' requires drivers to
options: slow down only slightly before continuing
increase their speed through the junction
ignore other approaching vehicles
come to a complete halt before proceeding
questions.explanation: The octagonal 'STOP' sign is a regulatory sign requiring drivers to come to a full stop and check for safety before proceeding.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: Pedestrians can contribute to reducing road traffic accidents by
options: walking on active highways instead of designated walkways
crossing roads at any point regardless of oncoming traffic
using designated pedestrian crossings and obeying traffic signals
ignoring traffic lights meant for pedestrians
questions.explanation: Pedestrians reduce accident risk by using marked crossings and obeying traffic signals, rather than crossing roads carelessly.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: Vehicle over-speeding is a major cause of road accidents mainly because it
options: is always safer on well-maintained roads
reduces a driver's ability to react in time to avoid a collision
improves a driver's control over the vehicle
has no effect on stopping distance
questions.explanation: Excessive speed reduces the time a driver has to react to hazards and increases stopping distance, significantly raising accident risk.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: Traditional rulers and community elders often play a valuable role in inter-personal relations by
options: mediating disputes and promoting reconciliation between conflicting parties
encouraging communities to avoid all forms of dialogue
refusing to engage with modern conflict resolution methods
escalating minor disagreements into larger conflicts
questions.explanation: Traditional leaders often hold significant respect and influence, making them valuable mediators in resolving communal disputes and fostering reconciliation.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: Democracy is best defined as a system of government in which
options: all decisions are made solely by unelected officials
power is derived from the people, typically through free and fair elections
power is inherited exclusively through a royal family
a single military leader holds absolute power
questions.explanation: Democracy is fundamentally a system in which political power and legitimacy come from the people, usually exercised through free elections.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: A key feature of democracy is the holding of
options: regular, free, and fair elections
no elections at all, with power inherited
elections controlled entirely by the military
elections only once in a lifetime for each citizen
questions.explanation: Regular, free, and fair elections are a defining feature of democratic governance, allowing citizens to choose and change their leaders.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: The democratic principle whereby decisions are generally made according to the wishes of the greater number of people is called
options: minority rule
military dictatorship
majority rule
absolute monarchy
questions.explanation: Majority rule means that decisions and electoral outcomes are generally determined by the preference of the larger share of voters or representatives.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: A system of democracy in which citizens directly participate in making laws and decisions, without elected representatives, is called
options: monarchical democracy
representative democracy
military democracy
direct democracy
questions.explanation: Direct democracy allows citizens to vote directly on laws and policies themselves, rather than through elected representatives.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: A system of democracy in which citizens elect representatives to make laws and decisions on their behalf is called
options: representative democracy
military rule
direct democracy
absolute monarchy
questions.explanation: Representative democracy, the most common modern form, involves citizens electing officials to govern and legislate on their behalf.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: A key pillar supporting democratic governance, providing citizens with organised platforms to contest for political power, is the
options: public corporation
political party
traditional council
civil service
questions.explanation: Political parties organise citizens around shared political goals, providing structured platforms through which candidates contest elections for public office.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: A key pillar of democracy responsible for interpreting laws and checking the excesses of the other arms of government is the
options: judiciary
legislature
electorate
executive
questions.explanation: The judiciary, through judicial review and impartial interpretation of the law, serves as a critical check on the powers of the executive and legislature.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: A key pillar of democracy that informs the public, investigates government actions, and holds leaders accountable is the
options: free press (mass media)
political party
traditional institution
civil service
questions.explanation: A free and independent press plays a crucial role in informing citizens and holding government officials accountable for their actions.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: The rule of law is best described as the principle that
options: laws apply differently based on a person's wealth or status
only ordinary citizens must obey the law
everyone, including government officials, is subject to and accountable under the law
the government may act outside the law when convenient
questions.explanation: The rule of law requires that all individuals, including those in government, are equally subject to and bound by the law.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: A basic principle of the rule of law is
options: the total absence of any written laws
special legal immunity for wealthy citizens
different courts and laws based on ethnicity
equality before the law for all citizens
questions.explanation: Equality before the law ensures that all persons, regardless of status, are treated equally under the same legal standards and protections.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: Another basic principle of the rule of law is
options: biased treatment favouring government officials
punishment without a fair hearing
secret trials with no legal representation
impartiality in the administration of justice
questions.explanation: Impartiality requires that justice be administered fairly and without bias, regardless of a person's position, wealth, or connections.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: A factor that can limit the effective operation of the rule of law in a country includes
options: corruption and undue political interference in the judiciary
a fully independent and well-funded judiciary
strong public trust in legal institutions
consistent and equal enforcement of laws
questions.explanation: Corruption and political interference can undermine judicial independence and fairness, weakening the effective operation of the rule of law.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: Civil society refers to
options: organisations and associations, independent of government, that represent citizens' interests
a country's armed forces
the executive arm of government alone
a group of elected legislators
questions.explanation: Civil society consists of voluntary, non-governmental organisations, such as NGOs and advocacy groups, that represent and advance citizens' interests.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: An example of a civil society organisation is
options: a non-governmental human rights advocacy group
a government ministry
the national police force
the country's central bank
questions.explanation: Non-governmental organisations advocating for human rights are a common example of civil society, operating independently of state control.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: A key role of civil society organisations in a democracy is to
options: replace the elected government entirely
eliminate the need for a free press
prevent citizens from voting in elections
monitor government actions and defend citizens' human rights
questions.explanation: Civil society groups play a watchdog role, monitoring government conduct, advocating for citizens' rights, and promoting accountability.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: Public service refers to
options: religious organisations providing spiritual guidance
the body of government employees responsible for implementing government policies and providing services
private businesses providing goods for profit
elected officials serving in the legislature
questions.explanation: The public service comprises career government employees who implement policy and deliver public services, distinct from elected political officeholders.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: A key characteristic of the public service is
options: temporary employment that changes with every election
active membership in the ruling political party
direct control over the passage of laws
political neutrality, serving any government in power impartially
questions.explanation: Public servants are expected to remain politically neutral, serving successive governments impartially regardless of which party is in power.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: Another key characteristic of the public service is
options: permanence, providing continuity in administration across different governments
complete anonymity with no accountability to the public
total independence from any form of government oversight
reliance solely on private funding rather than government budgets
questions.explanation: Permanence ensures that skilled public servants continue in their roles across changes in political leadership, providing administrative continuity.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: A common reason for performance shortcomings within the public service is
options: efficient and transparent service delivery systems
strong political neutrality among staff
excessive training and professional development opportunities
inadequate funding, corruption, and poor staff motivation
questions.explanation: Public service performance often suffers due to insufficient resources, corrupt practices, and low staff morale or motivation.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.text: Nigeria's Service Compact with All Nigerians (SERVICOM) initiative was established mainly to
options: transfer all government functions to private companies
improve the quality, efficiency, and accountability of public service delivery
abolish the public service entirely
reduce citizens' access to government services
questions.explanation: SERVICOM was introduced as a reform initiative to improve service standards, efficiency, and accountability within Nigeria's public service.
